title: SEO vs AEO: What's the difference and why it matters
headings: Do I need both AEO and SEO?
What are the key differences between AEO and SEO:
How do you measure success when it comes to AEO?
text: Staying visible in the era of AI requires structured content, schema, and AI-readiness. For years, SEO (Search Engine Optimization) has been the bedrock of online visibility, a meticulous craft of keywords, backlinks, and technical wizardry designed to rank highly on Google. But with the rapid growth of AI-driven search—think Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, and ChatGPT—the game is changing. Being number #1 on Google is still important, but we also need to consider how we show up in AI-generated answers, smart assistants, and summary panels. With this new reality it demands a new approach: Answer Engine Optimization (AEO). Your Content Management System (CMS) needs to be more than just SEO-friendly; it needs to be AI-visible. Join us in exploring how AEO differs from SEO, why it matters, and how us marketers can adapt. Is AEO replacing SEO? AEO, is not replacing SEO; it's evolving it. Think of it less as a hostile takeover and more as a sophisticated upgrade. The goal of traditional SEO is to drive organic traffic by relying on how well your content satisfies search engine algorithms and how effectively it matches user queries. AEO, on the other hand, is about optimizing your content so that AI models can easily understand and accurately present it in their responses. For us this means we have to shift our strategy beyond simple keywords and extend it to: Is AEO replacing SEO? AEO, is not replacing SEO; it's evolving it. Think of it less as a hostile takeover and more as a sophisticated upgrade. The goal of traditional SEO is to drive organic traffic by relying on how well your content satisfies search engine algorithms and how effectively it matches user queries. AEO, on the other hand, is about optimizing your content so that AI models can easily understand and accurately present it in their responses. For us this means we have to shift our strategy beyond simple keywords and extend it to: Structured content: Breaking down information into digestible, machine-readable blocks. Semantic markup: Using schema.org and other structured data formats to explicitly tell AI: AI what your content means, not just what it says. Entity-based optimization: Ensuring your content is associated with specific entities (people, places, things) that AI models can recognize and connect. AI-readable formats: Adapting content for various AI outputs, from concise summaries to conversational answers. In essence, SEO helps search engines find your content, whilst AEO helps AI understand and utilize your content. Both are crucial for visibility in 2025 and beyond. Do I need both AEO and SEO? Absolutely! It's not about picking between AEO and SEO; it's about bringing them together. Think of them as two essential parts of the same strategy, both working to make sure your brand gets found and understood. SEO is your foundation: This is what makes sure your website is technically sound, easy for search engines to crawl, and ultimately discoverable. Honestly, without a strong SEO strategy, your amazing content might never even get noticed by the AI models that could leverage it. AEO is your AI amplifier: Once your content is discoverable, AEO steps in to make sure AI can easily understand and use it. This means your valuable insights could pop up in AI Overviews, voice search results, and even chatbot responses, taking your reach way beyond just a click on a search engine results page. Ignoring either one means you're missing out on huge opportunities. A solid SEO strategy will keep driving traffic to your site, while a smart AEO approach will set you up for success. The top CMS platforms out there are the ones that help marketers master both! What are the key differences between AEO and SEO: S EO vs. AEO at a glance SEO AEO Primary Channel Google, Bing, Yahoo Google Ai Overviews, ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Claude Goal Rank high in search results Be referenced or cited in AI-generated answers Core Strategy Keywords, backlinks, technical SEO Structured data, semantic clarity, authoritative sources Content Format Web pages, blogs, landing pages Knowledge-based, concise, answer-driven content Measurement Metrics SERP rankings, organic clicks, dwell time Mentions in AI answers, citation tracking, conversational visibility User Journey Search→ Click→ Visit website Question→ AI answer→ Source mention or summary How do you measure success when it comes to AEO? While metrics like page views and organic rankings are still important, AEO brings some new and exciting ways to measure performance beyond traditional SEO metrics. AI visibility score: Think of this as a comprehensive metric that tells you how often and how prominently your content is showing up in AI-generated answers, summaries, and conversational interfaces. It's about being seen where AI is talking. Citation count & share of voice: This is all about tracking how frequently AI models are actually citing your website as a source. Even more, it measures what percentage of AI-generated answers in your specific niche are referencing your brand. Are you becoming an authoritative voice for AI? Direct answer & featured snippet presence: While these aren't entirely new, they become even more critical with AEO. Why? Because AI models frequently pull information directly from these highly visible search engine results features. Securing these spots is paramount. AI exposure rate: This is a powerful new metric that quantifies the likelihood of your content being discovered and utilized by various AI systems. It's about maximizing your content's reach within the AI ecosystem. Semantic relevance & entity recognition: We're talking about tools that dive deep into your content to analyze how well AI understands the core entities and concepts within it. This essentially tells you how "AI-ready" your content truly is. Traffic from AI referrals: As AI interfaces become more sophisticated and integrated into daily life, you'll start seeing new referral sources. These will directly indicate traffic that originated from AI interactions, showing you the tangible impact of your AEO efforts. It's just a matter of time until we see new tools emerge that can track AI visibility with the same precision we currently use for search rankings. But here's the thing: those who jump on this early are going to have a significant head start. This is where Optimizely CMS shines. With its strong focus on structured content, AI-readable schemas, and robust analytics, it's designed to help you track and optimize for these emerging AEO metrics. It's not just SEO-friendly; it's built to be AEO/GEO-ready as well. The Bottom Line It truly boils down to this: SEO is still vital for getting found in traditional search engines. But let's be real, more and more people are using AI chat tools, and that's where AEO steps in to keep your content visible within those generative responses. Think of AEO not as a replacement for SEO, but as its natural evolution. Just like SEO moved beyond simple keyword stuffing to focus on user intent, AEO is the next big step. For us marketers, this means a dual approach is essential. We need to maintain those strong SEO fundamentals, ensuring our websites are discoverable. But at the same time, we must enhance our content's semantic structure, boost its credibility, and clarify our data for these generative AI engines. If you can master both of these, you will be ahead of the curve. Visibility isn't just about being seen anymore; it's about being trusted by machines.

text: Search now happens in two places at once: Google's results pages and the AI-generated answers inside ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google's own AI Overviews. And winning only one of them leaves real traffic and brand visibility on the table. Because a page built purely to rank in organic search won’t necessarily get pulled into an AI-generated answer (and vice versa). In this guide, you'll learn what AEO (answer engine optimization) and SEO (search engine optimization) are, how they differ, where they overlap, and how to succeed with both. AEO vs SEO: what are the core differences? At the simplest level, AEO is about being included in AI-generated answers while SEO is about ranking in search engines. But the two overlap. Many of the same signals that help you rank in Google also increase your chances of being cited by AI tools. And AI features, like Google AI Mode , live in both worlds. Here's how AEO and SEO differ — and the similarities they share: AEO SEO Goal Get your content cited or mentioned in AI-generated answers (and in voice search) to grow brand awareness and drive traffic to your site. Rank high in organic search — including search engine results pages (SERPs) and AI-powered features like AI Overviews — to drive traffic to your site. User behavior Users ask questions and read or listen to the AI-generated answer. They might also explore the sources used to create the AI response (citations). Users browse SERPs and decide which link to click. They also explore AI-generated answers to satisfy their search intent and potentially click to learn more. User intent Get detailed information directly from the AI search engine. Navigate to a site for detailed information or get an instant response via a SERP feature . Discovery surface AI answers, citations, embedded URLs, brand mentions, and Google's AI features. Direct links, featured snippets, People Also Ask, local packs, knowledge panels, AI Overviews, and AI Mode. Success metric Increase in AI brand mentions , citations, or placements in AI-generated responses. Higher rankings and visibility across both search results and AI-powered features, leading to more organic traffic. Let’s go over what AEO and SEO are in greater detail. What is AEO? AEO (answer engine optimization) is a digital marketing strategy that helps make your web content easily discoverable by AI search engines like ChatGPT and voice assistants like Alexa. The goal of an AEO strategy is to have your content appear or be cited when someone asks AI a question related to your business, product, service, or industry. Because with 77% of ChatGPT users in the USA treating it like a search engine, and nearly 60% of consumers using AI tools to shop, AEO can drive discovery, trust, and conversions. For example, if you sell a project management tool for finance teams, you want your brand to appear when someone asks ChatGPT, " What's the best project management software for finance teams? " What is SEO? SEO (search engine optimization) is a digital marketing strategy that helps your website rank higher in search engine results like Google and Bing. SEO focuses on keywords, backlinks , content depth, and site structure to drive organic traffic and improve your visibility in the SERPs. At the same time, SEO strategies continually evolve to include SERP features like AI Overviews , carousels, featured snippets, People Also A sk boxes, knowledge panels, and more. How AEO and SEO work together AEO and SEO work together by making your content findable, authoritative, and quotable. SEO builds your domain authority and ensures your content is trustworthy, while AEO ensures that content is easier for AI systems to parse, understand, and cite. So, does ranking well on Google get you cited by AI? Partly. When we compared AI answers with Google's organic results, our research found: AI favors trusted domains : Strong organic rankings and authority make a domain more likely to be cited AI doesn't necessarily cite high-ranking pages : AI often pulls deeper subpages, blog posts, or documentation within trusted domains instead of the exact ranking URLs Overlap depends on the platform : Google AI Mode's sidebar shows lower overlap with Google's top 10, while its additional links have much higher overlap. Perplexity has the strongest alignment with Google, and ChatGPT the weakest, though it still leans on authoritative domains. Authority drives inclusion : AI consistently prioritizes domains with strong backlinks, authority, and visibility — even when it pulls different pages than Google's top results In short, AEO extends SEO rather than competing with it: the same fundamentals that earn a domain trust in Google's eyes are what make it worth citing in an AI-generated answer. How to succeed in both AEO and SEO There are many strategies to help you succeed in both AEO and SEO — from creating original content to building external signals and structuring your content for retrieval. Let's break those down in detail. 1. Create unique, research-backed content Creating unique, research-backed content sends positive signals to search engines and AI search platforms, as both reward content grounded in real experience that AI alone can't generate. So when planning your digital content, make sure you bring something original to the table — like personal experience, fresh data, or expert insights. For example, we conducted original research on whether backlinks still matter for AI. That post is one of the first results in organic search. The post also appears in AI Overviews. And is cited in AI search platforms like ChatGPT. To create content that boosts both SEO and AEO: Write from first-hand experience: Share what you've actually done, tested, or figured out through real work. Even small insights can help your content stand out. Use original data: Run surveys, document experiments, or pull insights from your own product. Unique stats and internal findings add credibility and increase the chances of being cited. Add author bios: Make it clear who's behind the content and why they're worth listening to. Mention each author's role, area of expertise, or hands-on experience. Quote experts: If you don't have direct experience, speak to someone who does. Bring in their insights, ideas, or frameworks. It adds depth and signals trust to both AI and human readers. 2. Build authority through brand mentions and backlinks Building authority through brand mentions and backlinks matters because search engines and AI search platforms favor sources that other trusted sites reference. In practice, this translates into attracting: Backlinks (links from other relevant websites that point to your content): Backlinks remain one of the core SEO ranking factors, and our research on the impact of backlinks for AI search found that they’re also associated with greater visibility in AI search Brand mentions (linked and unlinked mentions to your brand across trusted sites): Brand mentions are especially important for AI search platforms, which often rely on recognizable brands when generating answers As Alex Birkett noted in our webinar, both signals are critical if you want to succeed in SEO and AEO: Do backlinks still matter? Yeah, a hundred percent. They’re still an input vector for your website’s authority and page authority, and they’re important in both classic and LLM optimization. But brand mentions also play a big role — even unlinked ones — because with LLMs it’s more text-based: the model looks at the text around the prompt and whether your brand is mentioned there. What matters is being referenced across multiple trusted sources. Alex Birkett, Co-Founder of Omniscient Digital Here are a few tips that can help you earn more mentions and backlinks: Create content backed by original research and expert insights that others want to reference and link to Contribute expert commentary to blogs or media outlets in your niche Pitch guest posts to sites with high authority and strong reputation in your industry Work with writers who regularly contribute to credible publications and already have relationships with editors Collaborate with trusted brands or creators on co-branded content, original studies, or interviews that naturally lead to mentions and links For example, HubSpot frequently publishes original, expertise-driven content, like its annual State of Marketing Report , which features original research and essential industry data. The report's page has generated thousands of backlinks over the years: It also gets mentioned by various bloggers, outlets, and other relevant industry players: Creating this kind of content consistently has paid off in both channels: HubSpot has an extremely high AI visibility score , is frequently cited by AI search platforms, and draws millions of organic visits each month. 3. Use entities to strengthen topic relevance Using entities — clearly named concepts like people, companies, products, or places — strengthens topical relevance by helping search engines and AI match your page to relevant topics and queries. Google uses these entities as part of its Knowledge Graph — a database of facts about people, companies, products, and places. And AI search platforms like ChatGPT rely on consistent entity signals to make connections between prompts, topics, and brands. For example, writing about Amazon could mean the company or the rainforest. Adding terms like "Amazon Prime," "Jeff Bezos," or "ecommerce" makes it clear you're talking about the business. To effectively use entities in your content: Use consistent terminology for tools, frameworks, and products : Say "Google AI Overviews" every time instead of switching to "AIOs" or "Google AIOs" Include your brand and product names clearly : Place them near key points of value so search engines and AI systems connect your brand to what you offer Add related concepts and subtopics : If you're writing about Tesla, mention "electric vehicles," "Model 3," or "EV charging stations," and cover themes like pricing and safety Use examples and analogies that reinforce the topic : Comparing website architecture to a house blueprint works because both determine how easily people can find their way around For example: Could be better (inconsistent and generic) Good (entities, consistency, and clarity) "Our tool tracks rankings in Google SERPs and AIOs, plus AI mode and chatbots. You can also see which sources mention your site so you know where you're cited." "Our platform tracks rankings in Google SERPs and Google AI Overviews, plus visibility in Google AI Mode and ChatGPT. You can also see the citation sources used for your pages (e.g., Reddit, YouTube, G2), so you know where you're being referenced." 4. Structure your content for clarity Structuring your content for clarity helps search engines and AI search platforms understand relationships between concepts and determine what's most important on your page. In practice, this means leading each section with a concise, standalone answer before adding supporting detail, and organizing the rest of your content in a logical, hierarchical way with clear sections and formatting. To optimize your content structure for SEO and AEO (and users): Use clear hierarchical heading structure (H1, H2, H3) that creates logical topic relationships Place key information in strategic locations like the beginnings of paragraphs, sections, and documents Use ordered lists for processes/rankings and bulleted lists for related items Add structured data markup (schema.org) when possible to explicitly label content types like FAQs, products, or reviews Maintain consistent formatting throughout your content to reinforce structure For example, this Semrush article uses clear H2s and answers each heading's question in the first sentence of the section. It also breaks related items into bullet points, making the page easier for readers to scan and for bots to parse. It also uses numbered lists to outline steps and keeps formatting consistent, making complex information easier to follow. 5. Keep your content fresh Keeping your content fresh requires regular audits, as search engines and AI systems prefer citing up-to-date content. Fresh content is an important SEO ranking factor and is key to content quality, especially for pages where relevance changes quickly (e.g., news). Research also shows that AI search platforms have a clear preference for pages that are recent and trustworthy. That preference makes sense given how AI answers are built. Many of these platforms pull from live retrieval systems, so when two pages cover the same ground, the more recently updated one is more likely to get cited. Updating the publish date alone doesn't help — the content itself needs genuinely new information, current examples, or corrected details for that recency signal to mean anything. Here's what you can do to keep your content fresh and relevant: Update factual information, statistics, and examples with the most current data Refresh screenshots and visuals to reflect current interfaces and designs Add new sections covering recent developments in your topic area Remove or update references to outdated tools, methods, or practices Optimize for emerging keywords and changing search intent (the goal behind a search query) 6. Make your content extractable for AI answers Making your content extractable for AI answers means structuring each section so AI systems can pull it into an answer on its own, since they use specific passages rather than entire pages. To make your content easier for AI systems to lift and cite directly: Lead with a short, direct answer . Keep the first sentence of any section you want cited under roughly 40 words, and make it a complete, standalone answer — free of pronouns or references that only make sense alongside the rest of the paragraph. Use FAQ-style Q&A formatting for predictable follow-up questions . A heading phrased as a question, followed immediately by a direct answer, is easier for an AI system to match to a user's prompt than a heading like "Additional Considerations." Keep entity names consistent throughout a section . Switching between "Google AI Overviews," "AIOs," and "Google's AI feature" to describe the same thing makes it harder for AI systems to treat your mentions as references to the same entity. Semrush's Content Optimizer analyzes content for extractability signals like these and surfaces specific fixes. It works on existing pages too, so you can enter a URL and see what an older article needs. How to monitor AEO and SEO To monitor AEO and SEO, track your keyword rankings and AI prompt visibility side by side with tools like Semrush's SEO Toolkit and AI Visibility Toolkit . Using these tools regularly helps you understand what works (and what doesn't) so you can make strategic improvements. Key metrics to analyze include: Keyword rankings in organic search results Visibility in Google's AI features like AI Overviews and AI Mode AI Brand Mentions and rankings across AI search platforms Citation sources linking to your content AI Share of Voice against competitors for your priority topics Competitor performance across both channels For example, you can use our Keyword Magic Tool to find keywords to rank on Google — whether on SERPs or in AI features. For the AEO side, Prompt Research surfaces the prompts people ask AI platforms about your topic, so you know which questions to target before you write. You can then track the keywords you found in Position Tracking to monitor your Google rankings. For AI search, add your priority prompts to Prompt Tracking. It shows whether AI platforms cite, recommend, or ignore your brand for each prompt, so you can watch your AI visibility move the same way you'd watch your keyword rankings. Finally, use the AI Visibility Toolkit's Narrative Drivers report to see the specific AI prompts where you appear (or don't) versus competitors across AI Mode, ChatGPT, Gemini, and other platforms. By tracking both SEO and AEO side by side, you'll see where traffic is slipping and where AI is picking it up — so you can double down on the channels that drive results. Frequently asked questions about AEO vs SEO Will AEO replace SEO? AEO will not replace SEO — they will increasingly work together as complementary strategies. While SEO focuses on strategies to drive organic website traffic, AEO optimizes for AI-generated answers that may not always lead to clicks. The relationship is symbiotic — strong SEO fuels AEO success since AI systems favor content from trusted domains with solid organic rankings and authority. What is the difference between SEO, AEO, and GEO? SEO, AEO, and GEO aren't three separate, competing practices. SEO, together with Agentic Search Optimization (ASO), is the umbrella discipline for earning visibility everywhere people search. And AEO and GEO are two lenses within SEO and ASO. AEO and GEO target different layers of how AI systems find and use your content. Here's how AEO and GEO differ: AEO (answer engine optimization) focuses on the retrieval and citation layer — getting your existing content pulled into direct AI-generated answers and featured snippets in real time, as a user asks a question GEO (generative engine optimization) focuses on the model layer — how a brand appears in what an AI model already knows from its training data, independent of any single search or retrieval moment Both AEO and GEO roll up under SEO and ASO because the underlying inputs — authority, structure, relevance, and technical health — are the same ones that get a page ranked, retrieved, and cited in the first place. Can you optimize one page for both SEO and AEO? Yes, you can — and should — optimize one page for both SEO and AEO, by: Structuring content logically with proper headings Enriching it with original research and expert insights Using clear entities for topic relevance Keeping information current and comprehensive What tools can you use for SEO and AEO? Semrush offers dedicated toolkits for both SEO and AEO: The SEO Toolkit helps with keyword research , link building, site audits, and position tracking The AI Visibility Toolkit shows where and how your brand and content appear in AI-generated answers compared to your competitors You can also use Semrush's Content Toolkit to generate new content and optimize your existing drafts to rank in organic and AI search.

text: TL;DR: SEO improves visibility in traditional search results. AEO structures content so answer engines can present it as a direct answer. GEO focuses on whether AI-generated responses mention and cite your brand. The tactics overlap heavily: useful content, technical accessibility, clear structure, authority, and freshness support all three. What differs is how you measure visibility: rankings, direct answers, citations, mentions, and AI referral traffic. Key Takeaways SEO (Search Engine Optimization) improves visibility in traditional search results by making your site and content easier for search engines to find, understand, and rank. AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) structures content so answer engines can extract and present it as a direct answer. GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) focuses on visibility in AI-generated responses, including whether AI engines mention and cite your brand or content. SEO, AEO, and GEO tactics overlap heavily. Useful content, technical accessibility, clear structure, authority, and freshness can support all three. SEO, AEO, and GEO measure visibility through different signals. These include rankings, direct answers, citations, mentions, and AI referral traffic. Your CEO or founder has asked what you’re doing about GEO, but you already have an SEO strategy in place. The question is how much of that strategy needs to change. Most GEO and AEO tactics overlap with the SEO work you’re already doing. The outcomes are quite different though, and that changes what you need to measure. If you’re deciding whether to hire a GEO specialist, retrain your SEO team, or ignore this new acronym for now, start here. This article breaks down SEO, AEO, and GEO. You’ll learn where they overlap, where they differ, and how to go about your search strategy moving forward. What’s the difference between SEO, AEO, and GEO and what do they stand for? SEO focuses on making your website and content more visible in traditional search results and relies on content relevance, site structure, backlinks, and technical performance. AEO focuses on structuring content so search engines and AI systems can select it as a direct answer, rather than simply ranking it on a results page. GEO applies similar optimization principles to generative search. The term was introduced in a 2024 paper by researchers from Princeton University and Georgia Tech , which examined methods for improving a website’s visibility in generative engine responses. SEO AEO GEO What it stands for Search Engine Optimization Answer Engine Optimization Generative Engine Optimization Where the result appears Traditional Search Engine Results Pages (SERPs) Featured snippets (Position Zero), voice assistants, and “People Also Ask” boxes AI-generated responses across conversational AI platforms like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews What it optimizes Web pages, site structure, and content for search engine crawlers Content structure, so it’s suitable for direct answers, entities, and Knowledge Graphs Deep topical authority, brand narrative, and context for large language models (LLMs) Primary signal Quality content, E-E-A-T, topical authority, backlinks, and technical performance Thoroughly answered questions and clear content structure that makes it easy to sift through Citation optimization and multi-platform visibility (including third-party publications) How you measure it Traditional organic rankings, click-through rates, and organic traffic growth Selection as the direct answer (featured snippets or voice search) Probabilistic measurement through iterative testing, monitoring citation frequency, and tracking AI referral traffic Who owns it internally SEO Manager Technical SEO, Content Strategist PR, Brand Marketing, Head of Content How much of GEO is just good SEO? Most of GEO is built on the same fundamentals as SEO, including quality content, E-E-A-T signals, topical authority, clear structure, and content freshness . These elements can help both search and AI engines to find, understand, and trust your content. An analysis of SEO pioneer Greg Boser’s take on AI search puts it this way: “The core principles of implementing effective technical SEO fundamentals remain relevant, though the implementation may need adjustment.” Strong SEO can support AI visibility, but it doesn't guarantee it. While Google ranking is a useful predictor of which pages appear as sources in Google AI Overviews , ranking alone doesn’t explain every citation. A March 2026 study of 863,000 keywords found that only around 38% of AI Overview citations come from pages in the top 10 Google results. For a walkthrough of how each discipline works in practice, watch our explainer: SEO, AEO and GEO Explained: How Each One ACTUALLY Works (13:07) · Watch on YouTube 6 ways GEO and AEO genuinely differ from SEO GEO and AEO build on SEO fundamentals, but they add requirements around how AI answer engines source content . This is particularly relevant as brands begin exploring LLM SEO strategies. Where GEO and AEO differ from SEO comes down to six elements: 1. Citation optimization: get named as the source, not just ranked SEO focuses on getting pages to rank in search results. GEO and AEO add another goal: getting those pages selected and cited as sources in AI-generated answers. A page can rank well organically and still not appear in AI-generated answers. GEO therefore puts more emphasis on whether an answer engine can find, understand, and cite the information on your page. Clear claims, supporting evidence, and source-worthy content all make that easier. What to do: Review your core pages and make each important claim specific, self-contained, and easy for an answer engine to cite. 2. Multi-platform visibility: every engine returns a different answer set SEO focuses on visibility in search results, while GEO tracks brand mentions in AI answers across multiple answer engines that can draw on different sources. ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, and other answer engines don’t necessarily retrieve the same sources or mention the same brands. A page that performs well in one platform can have limited visibility in another, because each engine can use different sources and retrieval systems. So, optimizing for one channel doesn't give you a complete picture. What to do: Check your priority topics across the answer engines your buyers use and record which brands and sources appear consistently. 3. AI visibility measurement: there’s no rank to track SEO gives you relatively stable positions to monitor, while AI-generated answers can change between runs, even for the same prompt. That makes a single position an unreliable basis for AI visibility tracking . Instead, you need repeated prompts, consistent tracking, and enough observations to identify trends rather than treating one generated answer as a fixed result. What to do: Run the same priority prompts from a logged-out LLM at least three times and track: whether your brand appears where it appears and whether it gets cited See whether AI engines mention your brand Find out where your brand appears in AI-generated answers, and where it doesn't. Get your free visibility report 4. Consensus signals: one strong page isn’t enough SEO can concentrate authority around a specific page, whereas GEO benefits from consistent information about your brand across multiple relevant sources. Answer engines can combine information from several pages and domains when forming a response. If your website says one thing while reputable third-party sources describe your company differently, the engine might consider you unreliable. Consistent facts across your site and external sources give answer engines clearer information to work with. What to do: Search your brand across your site and major third-party sources, including your industry directories and review sites. Then fix outdated or conflicting information. 5. Third-party presence: Reddit and review sites carry your brand SEO has traditionally focused heavily on your own website and the links pointing to it. GEO also requires paying attention to where other people discuss and describe your brand. Answer engines use third-party discussions, reviews, forums, and other sources when answering questions about products and companies. For example, our Google AI Overviews citation data shows YouTube (about 37%) and Reddit (about 21%) among the most-cited domains. Your website can’t control most of those conversations, but you can monitor what information is available and address the gaps or inaccuracies. What to do: Search your brand on the third-party sites that influence your category and note the questions, comparisons, and descriptions that appear most often. Or use Searchable’s LLM citation tracking to find the sources AI trusts in your category. 6. Query length: prompts run far longer than keywords SEO often starts with short keywords, while AEO and GEO rely on longer, conversational prompts that include context, constraints, and multiple requirements. For example, a buyer might search Google for “CRM for startups,” but ask an answer engine for several CRM options for a 20-person SaaS company with a specific budget and integration needs. That longer prompt changes which information matters, because the engine has to find and weigh information against several conditions at once. What to do: Build prompt variations around your core topics, adding the audience, use case, constraints, and comparison criteria your buyers care about. Then cover those questions in your content. How to tell real AEO and GEO tactics from snake oil As AI search gains traction, more marketers are promoting tactics that promise to improve visibility in AI-generated answers. The challenge is separating strategies with a clear mechanism and evidence from tactics that mainly rely on hype. A credible AEO or GEO strategy should explain what it’s changing, how success will be measured, and what evidence supports the approach. John Mueller, Google’s Search Advocate, has said that search is never guaranteed , and Google’s own guidance warns that no one can guarantee a #1 ranking . The same limitation applies to AI-generated answers. At minimum, a marketer promising guaranteed citations or mentions should be able to explain what they can actually control and how they'll measure the result. When you evaluate an AEO or GEO strategy, use these guidelines: Do Layer GEO and AEO on top of your existing SEO strategy rather than treating them as replacements for SEO. Prioritize useful, relevant, well-supported content that can perform well in both traditional and AI search. Use a clear measurement process that tracks AI referral traffic, citation frequency, and conversion performance. Track how your brand appears across different AI platforms and prompts, since visibility can vary between them. Look for vendors who can show real case studies rather than vague promises. Don't Trust claims that guarantee rankings, citations, or mentions in AI-generated answers. Believe that SEO is dead or that traditional search fundamentals no longer matter. Treat GEO or AEO as a completely separate discipline that requires separate efforts. Accept services from vendors who can’t explain what they measure or how. Expect one optimization change to produce immediate, consistent visibility across AI engines. Where to start with GEO and AEO: a three-tier plan Start with your existing SEO foundation, then make your content easier for search engines to find, understand, and cite. Finally, measure whether those changes are increasing your visibility. We created this three-tier approach you can follow to help integrate GEO and AEO into your existing SEO strategy: Tier 1: Audit your technical SEO foundation First, check whether search engines and AI crawlers can access the pages you want them to find. Review your robots.txt file, indexing status, internal links, canonical tags, and any content that relies on client-side rendering . Then fix any pages that aren’t accessible or indexable. A strong technical foundation gives both traditional search engines and AI systems a better chance of discovering your content. If your most important pages can’t be crawled or indexed, optimizing the content on those pages won’t help. Tier 2: Review your content for citation-worthy answers After you've established a solid technical foundation, pick your most important pages and check whether they answer the questions your audience actually has. Answering yes to the following questions can help you increase AI search citations : Does the content provide clear, concise definitions? Does it give direct answers to your audience’s questions? Does it support claims with reliable, verified evidence? Does it include relevant examples? Can key passages stand on their own when extracted out of context? Pro tip: Prioritize optimizing the pages that already generate a decent amount of organic traffic or business value. Tier 3: Measure your visibility and iterate Finally, build a prompt set based on the questions your buyers are asking in AI engines and track how often your brand appears in the answers. Track: Which prompts produce mentions or citations Where your brand appears Which sources answer engines use alongside your content You can test a few prompts manually, but variations between platforms and individual runs make manual tracking unreliable at scale. Instead, use Searchable’s AI visibility analytics to track your brand across nine AI platforms at once. Frequently asked questions about GEO, SEO, and AEO Is GEO replacing SEO? No, GEO is an extension of your existing SEO strategy, not a replacement. Strong technical SEO, useful content, and authority still help AI engines find and understand your pages. GEO adds work focused on whether AI engines select your pages and brand as sources in AI-generated answers. Do I need to hire a GEO agency? Not necessarily. If your team already has solid SEO skills, it can usually handle the fundamentals of GEO by adapting existing content processes and adding AI visibility tracking and prompt research. Hiring an agency makes sense if your team doesn't have the resources or expertise to manage that work consistently. How long does GEO take to show results? GEO results can take weeks or months to appear, depending on what you’re trying to change. Improving how easily AI engines find and understand your content can happen relatively quickly, but building authority and third-party signals that influence which sources they trust takes longer. That’s why two weeks is usually too short to judge a GEO strategy. Track visibility over a consistent prompt set so you can separate real changes from normal variation. Ready to build your GEO & AEO strategy? Terms like GEO, AEO, and LLM SEO will continue to shift and evolve as we go. However, the core principles driving results stay the same. To get chosen by AI engines, your brand's content should be high-quality, have a clear structure, topical authority, and credibility signals. If you’re ready to elevate your GEO and AEO strategy , our AI search optimization guide is a good place to start.

GEO vs AEO vs SEO Guide 2026 Learn how generative engine optimization (GEO) and answer engine optimization (AEO) help your content get cited by AI search engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews. Last updated : October 8, 2026 In Short: Generative engine optimization (GEO) helps brands earn visibility and citations in AI-generated responses, while answer engine optimization (AEO) structures content to answer user questions directly. Traditional SEO focuses on organic search rankings and traffic. To optimize for all three, create authoritative content with clear headings, direct answers, original insights, and credible sources that search engines and AI platforms can discover and reference. While marketers were perfecting our SEO game, the search landscape shifted beneath our feet. AI tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google's AI Overviews are changing how search discovery works entirely. The numbers tell the story. Ahrefs found that AI overviews reduced click-through rates for top-ranking Google content by 58% (a jump from 34.5% last year). Why? Because Google gives users the information they need without requiring them to leave the search page. At the same time, users often now go directly to LLMs for answers they previously would have found on search. ChatGPT, for example, processes 2.5 billion prompts daily, 65% of which qualify as search. The platform has a 96% lower CTR than Google. The reality is that search is becoming zero-click. That can feel jarring for marketing teams that spend years establishing visibility with traditional SEO. But we've got good news. SEO is still important and impactful, and when it's paired with a strategy for generative engine optimization (GEO) and answer engine optimization (AEO), two new and essential components of modern AI search strategy, marketers can build on what they've already established while optimizing for the AI era. Already familiar with GEO and AEO? Jasper's purpose-built agents handle the execution: scoring your content's AI readiness, surfacing citation gaps, and generating FAQ content and schema markup that answer engines pick up. Explore Jasper's GEO Agent and Hub. Key Takeaways GEO improves content discoverability and citation opportunities in generative AI responses. AEO focuses on answering user questions directly in AI-powered search experiences. Traditional SEO provides the foundation for organic visibility and AI search optimization. Original research, credible sources, and clear content structure strengthen GEO and AEO efforts. AI search performance should be measured through brand mentions, citations, and AI referral traffic. What is generative engine optimization (GEO)? Generative engine optimization (GEO) is the practice of optimizing content so that LLMs like ChatGPT and Gemini cite it as a trusted source in their responses. To do this, it's first important to understand how LLMs source their answers. Unlike traditional search engines that provide a list of ranked links for users to parse, LLMs synthesize answers from multiple sources. LLMs look for content that's easy to parse and reference, and that has authority indicators showing it can be trusted. GEO works by structuring content intentionally to make it AI-friendly in these ways, with a focus on authority, clarity, and factual accuracy. Key GEO tactics include: Evidence-backed authority: Original research, verifiable statistics, and data-driven insights get cited more frequently than unsupported opinions. AI models prioritize factual, well-sourced information. Clear structure: Schema markup, descriptive metadata—including meta titles and descriptions ( Jasper's Meta Description Generator workflow produces click-optimized titles and descriptions at page scale)—organized headings, charts, and tables help models parse and accurately reuse your information. Transparency signals: Clear authorship, proper citations, and data provenance build credibility with AI systems. Models favor content where they can verify the source and expertise behind the information. What is answer engine optimization (AEO)? Answer engine optimization (AEO) formats content for AI search features like Google's AI Overviews, Bing Copilot, and Perplexity's instant answers. It structures content to appear in answer-first responses that users increasingly rely on in their searches. Instead of ranking pages, answer engines extract and present information directly within the interface. This means content must not only be optimized to rank through keywords or topical relevance, but also hyper-aligned with the questions users ask and the intent behind their searches. AEO ensures that content can be easily extracted and delivered in these environments, with a focus on clarity, relevance, and immediate usefulness. Key AEO tactics include: Directness over cleverness: Answer user questions clearly and immediately. Content that gets to the point quickly is more likely to be surfaced in answer-first results. Structure for extraction: Use formats like FAQs, bullet points, tables, and lists that align with how answer engines present information. Machine-readable language: Write in plain, precise language that's easy for AI systems to interpret. Avoid ambiguity, complex phrasing, or unnecessary jargon that could reduce extractability. How do GEO and AEO differ from traditional SEO? In practice, SEO, AEO, and GEO should operate as a complementary, three-layer strategy: SEO establishes baseline visibility across traditional search engines AEO ensures accessibility in answer-driven search features GEO positions content as trusted reference material for generative outputs GEO and AEO don't replace SEO. In fact, SEO lays the foundation for better success in AI search visibility. Nearly 40% of Google's AI Overviews, for example, rank in the top 10 organic search results, and nearly 70% rank in the top 100. So while AI widens the playing field outside of page one, top-ranking content is still a factor for AEO in particular. Dimension SEO GEO AEO Primary goal Improve organic search rankings and traffic Increase brand visibility and citations in AI-generated responses Surface direct answers to user questions Optimization focus Keywords, search intent, technical SEO, and page relevance Topical authority, original insights, and AI search discoverability Conversational queries, answer relevance, and content structure Content style Comprehensive, keyword-relevant content organized around search intent Context-rich content with original research and expert perspectives Concise, direct answers with question-based headings and clear formatting Authority signals Relevant backlinks, content quality, and demonstrated expertise Credible citations, original research, and third-party brand mentions Accurate answers, credible sources, and clearly attributed expertise Visibility metrics Keyword rankings, organic traffic, click-through rates, and conversions AI citations, brand mentions, share of voice, and AI referral traffic Featured snippet visibility, answer appearances, and AI answer citations How to optimize content for AI search engines 1. Establish brand authority with your content Content has to be engaging, but for AI to recognize and share it, it also needs to be clear, authoritative, evidence-backed, and clearly trustworthy. Expand your content design focus to include these important factors, and bake them into the way you create content both for your website and non-owned channels like social and PR. Back claims with original research, surveys, or industry benchmarks. Include verifiable statistics from reputable third-party sources. Cultivate brand mentions and validation from trusted forums and third-party platforms such as Reddit and Quora. Provide clear authorship for blog content with relevant expertise credentials. Cite primary sources and link to authoritative publications. Update content regularly to maintain accuracy and relevance. 2. Structure content for AI parsing Simple, straightforward structure is key for AI recognition. You want to format content in ways that makes it easy to extract, reference, and align with user search intent. You can do this by: Using intent-based headings that mirror how users phrase questions. Leading each section with clear definitions or direct answers to user questions. Following with scannable content such as bullet points, numbered lists, or short paragraphs. Applying relevant schema markup (FAQPage, HowTo, Product)— Jasper's FAQ Schema Generator workflow handles question-and-answer generation, AEO optimization, and JSON-LD markup in a single production run. Writing conversationally using natural language patterns. Writing conversationally using natural language patterns. 3. Optimize for different AI platforms Different AI engines surface content in unique ways. It's important to understand your key audiences and where they search, and format your content intentionally to optimize for all LLMs and search engines where you want to appear. A quick list to help you get started: ChatGPT : Structured formats like bullet points and FAQs are often lifted verbatim. Perplexity : Always includes citations; prioritize authoritative sources and original data. Google AI Overviews : FAQ/HowTo schema, short definitions, and visuals improve inclusion chances. Bing Copilot : Synthesizes from high-quality results; favors step-by-step guides and comparisons. Claude : Benefits from longer, coherent passages with clear explanations and supporting evidence. What are the benefits of AI search optimization? AI-first search is creating new opportunities for brands ready to adapt their strategies. A wider organic playing field AI has increased the potential to drive visibility to your brand without having to attain that once holy-grail top blue link on search. As zero-click searches rise, marketers have an opportunity to reframe their search strategies away from driving traffic. Instead, the focus shifts to increasing the authenticity and authority, and ultimately the visibility, of your brand to influence buyers before they even land on your website. Higher LLM conversions LLM optimization can make up for conversions lost to lower Google click-through rates. Semrush reports that the average visitor from LLMs converts 4.4x better than traditional search traffic. AI-referred visitors overall demonstrate stronger purchase intent. A social boost Social media marketing and user-generated content now have a greater impact than ever on AI search visibility. Platforms like YouTube, Reddit, and LinkedIn are the most frequently cited across AI engines, with each LLM showing its own preferences. Google tends to surface content from platforms like Facebook and Yelp, while ChatGPT frequently cites Reddit and Wikipedia, and Perplexity emphasizes sources like Reddit, LinkedIn, and G2. By investing in social presence and community-driven content on these platforms, you can gain a significant boost in their AI search presence. Future-proof visibility While it feels like AI is everywhere, we're still in the early stages of AI search and how it will change the overall search landscape. Adopting an AI search strategy now sets you up for better adaptability and continued visibility as trends and platforms evolve. Jasper connects AI search visibility intelligence to governed execution in one platform. Track your citation rate across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot, find the content gaps your competitors are filling, and ship brand-governed drafts that arrive on-brand and citation-ready. See how Jasper helps you get cited by AI. Frequently Asked Questions What is the difference between GEO, AEO, and SEO? The difference between GEO, AEO, and SEO is their primary optimization focus. Generative engine optimization (GEO) helps content gain visibility and citations in AI-generated responses. Answer engine optimization (AEO) structures content to answer user questions directly. Search engine optimization (SEO) improves organic visibility in traditional search results. The three approaches work together to support discovery across search experiences. How does generative engine optimization (GEO) work? Generative engine optimization (GEO) works by making content easier for AI search platforms to discover, understand, and potentially cite. It emphasizes original research, factual accuracy, authoritative sources, and clearly structured information. These practices help establish content as a useful reference for AI-generated answers, although citations are never guaranteed. How does answer engine optimization (AEO) work? Answer engine optimization (AEO) works by organizing content around the questions users ask and providing concise, relevant answers. It uses descriptive headings, direct explanations, and clear formatting to make information accessible to AI-powered search features and answer engines. How do you optimize content for GEO and AEO? To optimize content for GEO and AEO, research relevant audience questions and create accurate, comprehensive answers. Use descriptive headings, place direct answers near the beginning of sections, and support important claims with credible evidence. Add original insights and maintain clear internal links to strengthen content relevance and discoverability. Do you still need traditional SEO if you use GEO and AEO? Yes. Traditional SEO remains important because AI search platforms rely on accessible web content and established signals of relevance and authority. Technical SEO, content quality, and logical website structure support discoverability across traditional and AI-powered search experiences. GEO and AEO build on these foundations. How do you measure GEO and AEO performance? GEO and AEO performance can be measured through brand citations, mentions in AI-generated answers, AI referral traffic, and conversions. Track visibility for relevant queries across AI search platforms and compare results over time. Traditional SEO metrics, including rankings and organic traffic, provide additional context for evaluating overall search performance. How often should you update content for GEO and AEO? Content for GEO and AEO should be updated when information becomes outdated, audience questions change, or new research becomes available. Regular content audits help identify opportunities to refresh factual claims, improve answer clarity, and address emerging search intent.
